preconditions.expression: all(c in {'A', 'B'} for c in S)
preconditions.description: Every character in the input string S must be either 'A' or 'B'.
The length of S is between 2 and 5000, inclusive.
The first line of stdin is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10) representing the number of test cases.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (stdout.strip() in {'A', 'B'} or len(stdout.strip()) > 1 and all(c in {'A', 'B'} for c in stdout.strip()))
postconditions.description: The output for each test case is either '-1' or a valid string T composed of 'A' and 'B' characters.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (len(T_candidate := stdout.strip()) > 0 and any(all(S[i] == T_candidate[j] for j, i in enumerate(subseq)) for subseq in subsequences(S, T_candidate)) == 2)
postconditions.description: If the output is not '-1', the string T_candidate must appear exactly twice as a subsequence in S. The function subsequences(S, T) returns all possible subsequence index sets of T in S.
